sentences: A rainbow arches over wide green fields.
A young couple walks along a country track with their dog, and a herd of cattle heads home toward a house among the trees.
The house stands right at the end of the rainbow.
This is Landscape with Rainbow, painted in 1859 by the American artist Robert S.
Duncanson. It is oil on canvas, about 76 centimetres high and 133 centimetres wide.
Since 1983 it has belonged to the Smithsonian American Art Museum in Washington, D.
C. Duncanson was born around 1821 in Fayette, New York, into a family of free African Americans who worked as carpenters and house painters.
Around 1840 he moved to Cincinnati, Ohio.
Cincinnati was home to many abolitionists, people working to end slavery, and they bought his paintings.
The wealthy Nicholas Longworth asked him to paint eight large landscape murals in the entrance hall of his mansion.
That house is now the Taft Museum of Art.
In 1853 Duncanson travelled to Europe to study the Old Masters.
Now look at the two people on the path.
The man, in plain country clothes and a hat, points toward the house.
The woman in a red dress lifts her hem a little as she walks.
The museum says the cattle heading home show people living in harmony with nature.
Look up at the sky.
The light of the setting sun falls across the pasture, and above it the rainbow forms a wide arc.
The land recalls the area around Cincinnati and Covington, Kentucky, just across the river.
The Ohio River between them divided a slave state from a free state.
Two years earlier, Frederic Church had won great praise for Niagara, with its own rainbow over the falls.
Duncanson boldly took on the same subject.
When the painting was first shown, a reviewer called it "one of the most beautiful pictures painted on this side of the mountains."
The museum reads the picture as a last hope for peace before the Civil War began.
As the war went on, Duncanson left Cincinnati for Montreal in Canada.
He died in 1872.
On Inauguration Day in January 2021, this painting was displayed at the U.
S. Capitol. The Taft Museum of Art has announced a retrospective of more than 80 of his works, opening in fall 2027.
Step back and see the whole landscape.
In a year when war was drawing near, a painter showed two people walking toward a home at the end of a rainbow.
Today, think about where your own rainbow ends, and take one small step toward it.
